title: Invalid send channels fail silently while invoke channels report an error
reasoning: `send` drops invalid channels without throwing, returning a rejected promise, or otherwise signaling failure, while `invoke` rejects invalid channels with a clear error. Renderer callers can therefore believe a fire-and-forget command was accepted even when it was blocked by the preload whitelist, which makes IPC wiring mistakes hard to detect and can produce stuck UI flows with no observable failure path.
recommendation: Make invalid `send` channels fail explicitly, for example by throwing an `Error` or returning a boolean/status that callers can check, and keep the behavior documented consistently with `invoke`.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for invalid IPC channel handling, and the shown package scripts only indicate general Jest coverage rather than a specific preload contract test.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a preload IPC test that calls `window.ipc.send` with an invalid channel and asserts a deterministic failure signal, plus a valid-channel case that still delegates to `ipcRenderer.send`.
minimumFixScope: Update `frontend/src/preload.js` invalid-channel handling for `send` and add focused tests for valid and invalid send paths.
